intent.creator_purpose: Present the integrated ACS hotload installation as a comprehensible local working arrangement for agents on an ongoing software project, without confusing the pack's value with a single component's scope.
intent.user_need: An individual builder wants to return to their actual project rather than repeatedly reconstructing agent context, ownership, review rules and handoffs between work sessions.

audience.actor: Individual technical builder maintaining a real project with multiple AI agents across sessions
audience.job: Make progress on the project while keeping several AI agents aligned on responsibilities, prior decisions and safe handoffs
audience.trigger: Returning to a long-running repository or adding more agents after earlier sessions
audience.workaround: Rereading prior conversations, manually restating decisions and rules, assigning and checking ownership, and reconciling output

position.promise: Give a long-running AI-assisted project a shared way of working so its builder can focus attention on making progress rather than continually rebuilding handoffs.
limitations: Intended attention benefit, not independently measured time savings or demonstrated customer outcomes
Requires a compatible, configured repository and pinned component prerequisites; no guaranteed one-click installation
ACS owns coordination; PCM, OIO and CGM remain distinct source-owned components of the integrated installation
Not a hosted service, autonomous decision-maker or automatic recovery of every prior chat
This page's illustration or walkthrough would not itself install, mutate a repository or authorize agent operations

buyer_journey.belief_change: Recognize that maintaining agent handoffs can become a second task that competes with project work
buyer_journey.message: You came to build something. The handoffs shouldn't become the main job.

buyer_journey.belief_change: Recognize repeated context, ownership and acceptance work as one pattern worth addressing
buyer_journey.message: The rules and decisions need somewhere better to live than the last chat.

buyer_journey.belief_change: Understand the integrated pack is local repository-level operating structure, not a hosted agent product
buyer_journey.message: One installable working surface, attached to the repository.

buyer_journey.belief_change: Understand what coordination, continuity, issue provenance and readable content each contribute
buyer_journey.message: Distinct pieces; one explicitly versioned way of working together.

buyer_journey.belief_change: Understand a real setup has prerequisites, verification and incomplete/partial states
buyer_journey.message: Inspect what gets wired, what is required and whether setup is complete.

buyer_journey.belief_change: Know exactly what the software does not promise, increasing informed trust
buyer_journey.message: The pack establishes process and records; it does not replace human judgment or guarantee project outcomes.

buyer_journey.belief_change: Know a safe next step and what that step is allowed to change
buyer_journey.message: Explore the installation safely before acting in your own repository.

ux_tasks.scenario: Visitor opens a proposed informational walkthrough of the installed working surface and inspects module responsibilities without touching their repository.
ux_tasks.success: Visitor can identify each source-owned module and correctly explain that the walkthrough does not execute an installer.

ux_tasks.scenario: Visitor follows a secondary link to source-pinned installation requirements for later local review.
ux_tasks.success: Link opens the public documented prerequisites without implying that a web click installed anything.

service_touchpoints.visible: Conceptual read-only explanation of the repo-level ACS hotload pack; clearly tagged as not executing setup
service_touchpoints.backstage: Intended client-side presentation only; no target repository, credential, issue mutation or installation subprocess
service_touchpoints.limitation: Candidate interaction; not implemented and not behaviorally verified. Must test passive network and write safety before acceptance.

service_touchpoints.visible: Explicit 'Read setup requirements' navigation to publicly documented source-owned installation prerequisites
service_touchpoints.backstage: Ordinary browser link to a pinned GitHub documentation page; no repository mutation intended
service_touchpoints.limitation: Actual URL resolution and link semantics not yet browser verified.

creative.headline: Build with agents. Stop managing every handoff.
outline: Recognition: builder losing attention to recurring coordination
The recurring extra job: reorientation, ownership, approval, explainability
Product reveal: a shared repository-level working surface
How it works: ACS / PCM / OIO / CGM, each with its real authority
The install experience: prerequisites, verify, READY/PARTIAL accurately distinguished
Boundaries: human control, real prerequisites, no fabricated metrics
Explore safely: read-only walkthrough or pinned requirements link

visual_roles.purpose: Human and actual project are the center; agents are supporting context, not emotional protagonists
Few sequential handoff snapshots in one project, without invented customer time savings or false live records
Repo-centered install surface illustrating how an explicit versioned operating contract attaches to a project
Four source-owned functions clearly labeled without claiming ACS wrote PCM, OIO or CGM
Conceptual setup and verification states, visibly examples rather than fabricated real logs
Plain-language limits legible in the normal page flow, not a scary compliance table
A distinguishable no-write informational action and real-documentation alternative

acceptance_tests: First-time intended builder can paraphrase the human coordination burden and what ACS installs without coaching
Hero and page remain understandable without animation, sound or decorative media
Integrated pack scope is accurate: ACS coordination, PCM continuity/governance, OIO issues, CGM content guidance
No claimed measured savings, live customer story, autonomous decision making, universal installation or phantom approval
Every source-backed claim has pinned provenance; historical CGM requirements are not automatically current successor capabilities
All actions disclose their behavior; a read-only walkthrough never attempts repository or external write operations
Link and interaction states are tested on mobile and desktop; keyboard focus, semantics and reduced motion are reviewed
Real running ABA output preserves approved wording and story; semantic concerns return to PEF rather than being patched by CSS
Version A remains immutable; Version B is generated into an isolated candidate environment only after owner acceptance
forbidden_inherited_patterns: ACS represented as merely a PCM continuation or merely an agent assignment tool
Process/provenance tables or architecture jargon as primary human hero
Invented invoice morning or fabricated customer outcome with fake precision
First-screen giant feature matrix, glowing robot imagery, meaningless cartoon agent parade
Text baked into visuals before the words have been approved
Preview button falsely suggests real installation, live running tasks or existing repo changes

cta.label: Explore what gets installed
cta.side_effects: Proposed: none; informational client-side walkthrough, not yet implemented or tested

review.notes: Only Q1 lead audience has been selected by the owner, recorded in CMF issue #1. Q2 benefit framing and Q3 actual CTA behavior remain blocking. Positioning D4 and D5, all buyer scenes, S3/S4/S5 creative gates, and rendered results are unapproved. This is not a build instruction.
